rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changes '4' to '5' only within a comment string ('// Store 4 floats at once' → '// Store 5 floats at once'). Comments are stripped during CUDA compilation. The actual store operation '*reinterpret_cast<float4*>(&output[idx * 4]) = out;' remains unchanged - it still writes exactly 4 floats via float4 to output[idx*4].
rounds.survival_reason: This mutation only affects comment text in the CUDA source code. The string '// Store 4 floats at once' was changed to '// Store 5 floats at once', but this is purely a documentation change with zero semantic effect. During CUDA compilation, comments are completely removed, so both the original and mutant compile to byte-identical PTX/SASS code. The actual store instruction still writes exactly 4 floats (via float4 struct) to the output buffer at position idx*4. Since the compiled kernels are identical, no input can ever produce different outputs between original and mutant. This explains why Layer 2 testing showed bitwise-identical outputs across all 112 rounds.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable because the mutation is in a comment, which has no effect on compiled code. The mutation testing tool incorrectly identified this comment text as a numeric constant. No input value strategy can distinguish kernels that compile to identical machine code.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should implement comment detection in CUDA source strings to filter out mutations to non-executable text. The const_perturb operator should verify that the identified constant is in executable code, not within a // or /* */ comment block. This false positive wastes testing resources on fundamentally equivalent code.
